title: Household Cap on Courtesy Permit Fees: Student Transportation Services
content:
Student Transportation Services caps the courtesy permit fees charged to one household in one school year at the household permit fee cap of the fee table (480.00 USD for every transportation type), counted after meal-status waivers.

**Rule.** When the household's courtesy permit fees already charged this school year, net of their waiver and cap credits, together with this fee net of its own meal-status waiver, exceed the cap, the excess is credited on this fee as a household cap credit. The fees already charged are the permit fees on the household's other transportation assignments of the same school year that posted earlier, less the free-meal waiver, reduced-price meal waiver and household cap credits against them. The cap credit is that excess, and never less than zero.

**Timing and scope.**
- The cap is computed from fees posted earlier. A fee posted later never changes a cap credit already posted.
- Replacement bus pass fees never count toward the cap.

## Condition and result

| Fees already charged this school year, net | This fee, net of its own waiver | Total against the 480.00 cap | Household cap credit on this fee |
|---|---|---|---|
| 240.00 | 135.00 | 375.00 | none |
| 375.00 | 135.00 | 510.00 | 30.00 |
| 480.00 | 67.50 | 547.50 | 67.50 |

(All rows are hypothetical households. In the last row the household had already reached the cap, so the whole net fee is credited.)

## Points of judgement

- **Which fees count.** Only courtesy permit fees of the same household and the same school year, on its other assignments, posted before this one.
- **What happens later.** A fee posted after this one is capped on its own posting and leaves this fee's cap credit as it stands.
